title: Remission = ceasing to be liable to punishment—requires repentance and faith
source_text: XI. Quod manifestum fiet, si diligenter attendamus quid sit, & qua in re consistat remissio peccatorum quae, quoad substantiam, idem est cum peccatoris justificatione. Remittuntur enim alicui peccata, quum cessat esse poenae propter peccata obnoxius. Atque idem plane sunt remissionem peccatorum consequi, & desinere esse poenae peccato debitae obnoxium. Jam autem nemo definit obnoxius esse poenae quam admissa peccata merentur, priusquam illa per veram poenitentiam derelinquat, & ad Dei misericordiam in Christo confugiat. Nam lex Dei est firma & stabilis, & in verbo ejus saepius inculcata, quod quicunque peccato indulget, nec ab eo per veram ad Deum conversionem recedit, judicio & irae divinae obnoxius manet. Quo pertinet illud Davidis, Non habitabunt injusti ante oculos tuos. Psal. 5. 6. Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem. Vultus autem Domini super facientes mala. Psal. 34. Item illud Domini nostri Jesu Christi, Nisi poenitentiam habueritis, omnes similiter peribitis. Et, Qui non credit in Filium non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum. Quamdiu ergo aliquis in peccato perseverat, necdum ad Deum conversus est, & fide Christum Redemptorem amplexus, tamdiu objectum est odii & irae divinae, & certa Dei lege perditioni aeternae obnoxius. Ac proinde in eo statu peccata nondum illi remissa sunt. Nam cui Deus peccata remisit, illum amplius odio non habet, nec illum vultu irato aspicit; aut est illi propter peccatum iratus. Nec amplius versatur talis in damnationis aeternae periculo, aut reatum ejus in se habet.
pass_a_gloss: This will become clear if we carefully attend to what remission of sins is, and in what it consists—which, as to substance, is the same as the sinner's justification. For sins are remitted to someone when he ceases to be liable to punishment because of sins. And it is plainly the same thing to obtain remission of sins and to cease to be liable to the punishment due for sin. Now no one ceases to be liable to the punishment that committed sins deserve before he forsakes them by true repentance and flees to God's mercy in Christ. For God's law is firm and stable, and often pressed in his word, that whoever indulges sin and does not withdraw from it by true conversion to God remains liable to divine judgment and wrath. To this belongs David's word: The unjust shall not dwell before your eyes (Ps 5:6). You hate all who work iniquity. The face of the Lord is against those who do evil (Ps 34). Likewise our Lord Jesus Christ's word: Unless you repent, you will all likewise perish. And: Whoever does not believe in the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him. Therefore as long as someone perseveres in sin, is not yet converted to God, and has not embraced Christ the Redeemer by faith, so long is he an object of divine hatred and wrath, and by God's sure law liable to eternal perdition. And so in that state sins are not yet remitted to him. For the one to whom God has remitted sins he no longer hates, nor looks on with an angry face, nor is angry with him because of sin. Nor does such a one any longer stand in danger of eternal damnation, or have its guilt in himself.
pass_b_english: Remission means ceasing to be liable to sin's punishment—same substance as justification.
While one persists in sin without conversion and faith, wrath remains; sins are not yet remitted.

choices.why: Equals release from liability to punishment.
